runners_data.name: Yanifer
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent racer with solid heavy-ground and soft-ground experience (6 runs in similar conditions), but a recent record of 9-0-0-4-0 raises serious concern about consistency; trainer Harriet Bethell in fair T14 form at 3/9 and Oisin McSweeney takes the ride, but the prominent berths are congested and this horse needs a clean run.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Yanifer nonetheless tops our ratings, if only narrowly, and having run over today's trip and conditions before, he arrives fit on a 14-day turnaround carrying 140 lb from stall four — the fourth placing two starts back is his best recent showing.

runners_data.name: Metal Merchant
runners_data.note: Sean Levey partners this hold-up specialist for John Butler, whose stable sends two runners today; 24 days since last run is not a concern, but only 5 qualifying runs in similar going conditions suggests limited heavy-ground exposure — his natural rear-of-field style is perfectly suited to the anticipated contested-pace race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Metal Merchant shaped with some promise when fourth two starts back, and with experience over today's trip and going he retains claims at a mark of 82 — though he is winless in his last five starts and that ninth last time out is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Final Night
runners_data.note: Consistent placed record (2-2-6-3 in recent starts at the trip) makes Final Night one of the more reliable prominent types in this field; David Egan is a high-quality booking, and the horse's 24-day freshener for the same Butler yard could sharpen a horse that ran on soft ground last time — no headgear concerns, though heavy ground is a marginal unknown with only one comparable run.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Final Night has been runner-up three times in recent form without converting, and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip before and 24 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Military Leader
runners_data.note: The most in-form prominent runner in the field with five consecutive top-three finishes including a win, blinkers fitted throughout that sequence, and two placed efforts on soft ground backing up his heavy-going claims; Paul Mulrennan rides for the well-placed Phillip Makin yard (T14: 2/13) and at OR 82 he carries joint-top weight but arrives with clear momentum.|
runners_data.comment: Military Leader won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims, but carrying 137 lb from stall 8 and ranked fifth of twelve in the field suggests he faces a stiff enough task to justify a midfield projection.

runners_data.name: Caim
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed pace-setters and a three-year-old with strong heavy-going form (3 from 4 in similar conditions including a win on soft and places on softer); Daniel Tudhope is a smart booking for Edward Bethell and Caim arrives 16 days fresh — the key question is whether Crown Office pushes him into an unsustainable early gallop, costing him the finish.|
runners_data.comment: Caim shaped with plenty of promise when finishing second three starts back and a winner four starts back, and she returns here on a quick 16-day turnaround with experience over today's trip; the 137 lb burden is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Miletus
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for James Keane (T14: 1/1, very small sample) with headgear (tongue-tie and blinkers fitted); only 5 qualifying runs in similar going conditions and limited recent form at the trip give cause for pause, though the placed record on soft (3 hits from 5 similar-going runs) provides a baseline.|
runners_data.comment: Miletus won three starts back and was third four starts back, showing he has the ability to mix it in these grades, but back-to-back fifths since suggest he is struggling to recapture that form; has run over today's trip and returns after 36 days off carrying 136 lb from stall ten.

runners_data.name: Jungle Ruler
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent racer for Michael Appleby with a consistent placed record but no win from six recent starts; two qualifying runs on soft going (both placed) offer some heavy-ground encouragement, though Clifford Lee takes a ride on a horse that has never quite converted form into victory — the congested prominent group makes life harder.|
runners_data.comment: Jungle Ruler has been a model of consistency, finishing in the top five in each of his last six starts with a second last time out and a third two starts back, and his experience over today's trip bolsters his claims at a useful 94 on our rating; the chief concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Crown Office
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand's mount for William Haggas (T14: 11/52, excellent in-form trainer) is the second confirmed pace-setter; Crown Office won on soft ground (OR history) and has placed at listed level, but his recent form has been patchy and he arrives 37 days fresh — if he can't match Caim's stride, he may fade badly on heavy ground.|
runners_data.comment: Crown Office has found the first three three times in his last five starts, and his speed figure of 79 sits well below the level required here, making him hard to fancy ranked ninth of twelve; he does carry a light weight from stall one and has run over today's trip, which are slim consolations.

runners_data.name: Monoceros
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Iain Jardine ridden by Andrew Mullen, arriving 38 days after his last start; the question-mark run in his history adds uncertainty, but a placed effort on soft ground and a consistent mid-pack finishing style suit the anticipated pace scenario — at OR 81 he is not without a chance if gaps appear late.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Monoceros does at least return here with distance experience and 38 days of freshness, though a pulled-up run among recent efforts and a mark of 81 give cause for caution from stall three.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: Loughnane's filly has won three of her last five runs, all at this trip and course combination (three wins on good at 8f), but her true style is prominent/front-running and the over-subscribed pace map means Laura Pearson will likely have to take a hold and race out of role in midfield — her soft-going record is limited (one run, 6th) and the style compromise is a genuine handicap here.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, The Sweet Escape faces a stiff ask against this field, yet his recent form is genuinely eye-catching: a winner last time out and winners three and four starts back, with a runner-up finish two starts back adding consistency, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Bearin Up
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up type has been dropped back in trip from 10f to 1m and arrives 15 days fresh; soft-ground placed form exists (3 qualifying runs including a place) and Duran Fentiman is a competent partner — the step down in distance might sharpen his finishing effort, and his natural rear style is ideally positioned for the anticipated race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Bearin Up arrives on the back of an unplaced effort and faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip and two wins in her last six starts show she is capable of better.

runners_data.name: Kindest Nation
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's five-year-old wears a visor for the first time (hg:v), which is worth noting as a potential sharpener; hold-up style suits the pace scenario but his recent form reads 4-9-6-3-0 in varying conditions and only 4 qualifying runs in similar going — the visor is the key angle to monitor in the paddock and at the start.|
runners_data.comment: Kindest Nation shaped with promise when third last time out, and her distance and going experience are in her favour, but she has been winless in her last five starts and her rating of 83 suggests she faces a stiff task from stall nine carrying 127 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Caim and Crown Office are confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead from flag, creating a genuinely contested gallop over Haydock's flat mile on heavy ground — energy will be expended early and the pace is unlikely to be false. Five runners (Yanifer, Final Night, Military Leader, Miletus, Jungle Ruler) are all chasing the prominent berths behind those two pace-setters, meaning the middle portion of the race will be congested and traffic danger between the two-furlong and three-furlong markers is a real threat. The Sweet Escape is a natural prominent racer but, with the prominent positions already over-subscribed, is mapped to midfield and will almost certainly race out of its preferred role, discounting its effectiveness. On heavy ground over a mile with a contested pace and a compressed prominent group, this race shape strongly favours horses with a genuine hold-up or late-running profile who can avoid the anticipated traffic and pick up ground in the straight — Metal Merchant, Monoceros, Bearin Up, and Kindest Nation are the style profiles that benefit most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Caim and Crown Office burn each other off early and the prominent group gets caught in traffic, genuine hold-up runners finish powerfully through a tiring field on heavy ground.
scenarios.body: The contested early gallop drains the leaders and the prominent cluster, leaving the straight clear for those who settled well in rear; heavy ground amplifies the attrition effect and rewards the most efficient galloping styles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not injurious and the prominent group (Military Leader, Final Night) settle in behind the leaders without traffic trouble.
scenarios.body: Military Leader's strong recent form (five consecutive places including a win) and heavy-ground suitability via blinkers makes him the most dangerous prominent runner if he gets a clean run; Final Night's consistent placed form at the trip also keeps him in the picture throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters, most likely Caim, establishes clear command early and the race develops into a stamina test that suits a single leader.
scenarios.body: Caim's heavy-going form is excellent (3 from 4 in similar conditions) and if Crown Office fails to match him stride for stride from the gates, Caim could control tempo and simply gallop rivals into the ground down the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Traffic Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent over-subscription creates a bunched scrimmage two to three furlongs out, with multiple runners checked or impeded and the race producing a scrambled, unconventional result.
scenarios.body: In this scenario a horse that manages to find daylight on the outer late, regardless of style, could emerge — Bearin Up (stepping back in trip) and Kindest Nation (if visor sharpens response) are the types most likely to benefit from opportunistic late gaps if the main group implodes.

watchPoints.text: Caim and Crown Office will fight for the early lead — if both are allowed to bowl along together unchallenged from the gates, the pace could become genuinely injurious on heavy ground and both may fold two furlongs out, leaving the race wide open for closers.

The five prominent runners (Yanifer, Final Night, Military Leader, Miletus, Jungle Ruler) chasing the same two or three positions create a serious traffic risk between the 2f and 3f markers — any runner caught in a pocket at that point could be fatally compromised even if travelling well.

The Sweet Escape is a natural prominent/front-running type forced into a midfield role by the overcrowded pace map — if Laura Pearson attempts to push forward regardless, she adds further chaos to an already congested prominent group in the early stages.

Military Leader carries joint-top weight (137lbs) alongside Final Night and Caim on genuinely heavy ground — if the ground is testing stamina severely, the weight burden on the most prominent runners could undermine even the best-form horses in the closing stages.

Crown Office (Haggas, T14: 11/52) is the better-credentialled of the two pace-setters on paper, but arrives 37 days fresh — watch him in the paddock and at the start for any signs of ring-rustiness before his contested early duel with Caim sets the race's shape.
